title: How to make furniture plans with AI from a sketch
heading: How to make furniture plans with AI from a hand sketch
description: Turn a photo of your furniture sketch into a 3D model, workshop drawings, a cut list and a shopping list with AI, without CAD skills. Step by step in free SOMA.
summary: A hand sketch of a low shelf on casters becomes a plywood panel construction with workshop drawings, a cut list and a shopping list, made by SOMA AI in SOMA.

video.title: From Hand Sketch to Furniture with SOMA AI: No CAD Skills Needed (Free & Open Source)

chapters.label: Add a door with Mark up

answer: Take a photo of your sketch, import it into SOMA and ask SOMA AI, the agent built into SOMA, in plain words to turn it into furniture made of wooden boards. It asks about anything unclear, then builds a 3D model board by board. On request it makes workshop drawings with all dimensions and a cut list and shopping list as an Excel file. Check the sizes before you cut any wood.
need: SOMA, free and open source, for Windows, macOS or Linux.

A sign-in for SOMA AI: a ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan, or an API key from Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter or OpenCode. SOMA is free, the AI runs on your plan or key. The cheapest way to start is an OpenCode Go subscription for about $10 a month.
A photo of your sketch, taken with your phone. Write the main sizes on it, for example width and height in cm.
A spreadsheet app such as Excel or LibreOffice Calc to open the cut list.

steps.title: Start a new model and bring in your sketch
text: Click New model on the start page and save it under a name; in the video it is Sideboard. Click the SOMA AI tab on the right and pick a model. The video uses GPT-6.1 Sol.

Click Import and pick the photo of your sketch. It goes into the model folder. Click it to open it, then click Send to agent. The sketch goes into the chat, ready for your message. In the video the sketch shows a low shelf on casters, 80 cm wide and 60 cm high, with a middle shelf and a divider in the middle, so four compartments.

steps.title: Describe the furniture in plain words and answer the questions
text: Write what you want, as you would tell a carpenter. No CAD terms needed. Say that you want to build it from wooden boards, and if you may want other sizes later.

SOMA AI looks at the sketch first. If something is unclear, it asks. In the video it asked four questions on one card: does the height include the casters, which board material, what goes on the shelves, and what casters to use. Click the answers that fit and send them. The video picks 60 cm including casters, 18 mm plywood, ornaments and light storage, and placeholder casters.
steps.prompt: This is my sketch of a low shelf on casters for my flat, sizes in cm. Please turn it into real furniture made of wooden boards that I can build in my workshop. I might want it in other sizes later. Ask me about anything that is unclear before you start.

image.alt: SOMA AI's question card next to the 3D view: whether the 60 cm height includes the casters, which board material (18 mm plywood, solid wood or MDF), and what the shelf will mainly hold

steps.title: Look at the shelf SOMA AI built
text: Then SOMA AI plans the boards and builds the model. This takes a few minutes; in the video it worked for 4 min 19 s.

The result is a real panel construction in plywood: two sides, top and bottom, the middle shelf, two dividers, a thin 6 mm back panel, and placeholders for the four casters. Every board is its own part in the structure tree. Click one in the 3D view and SOMA shows which board it is.
To look at the model, use the viewing tools above the 3D view. They change nothing. Explode pulls the boards apart, so you see how the shelf goes together.

image.alt: The plywood shelf in the 3D view with the structure tree open: Top, Bottom, Left side, Right side, Middle shelf, Lower divider, Upper divider, Back and the caster placeholders, and SOMA AI's summary on the right

steps.title: Ask for workshop drawings
text: Ask for drawings in one sentence. SOMA AI lays out every board with its dimensions. In the video it worked for about 8 minutes and made 10 A3 sheets: the assembly, one sheet per board, and assembly instructions.
Open Drawings in the sidebar on the left to see all sheets. They show the views with all the main dimensions, ready to print or to take into the workshop on a tablet.
steps.prompt: Make workshop drawings of the shelf with all the dimensions I need to build it.

image.alt: The Drawings tab with sheet 1 of 10, Shelf assembly: front and side views with dimensions such as 800 wide, a 3D view and a table of boards with their finished sizes, and the other sheets on the left

steps.title: Get a cut list and a shopping list
text: Ask for an Excel file with every board and a second sheet with everything you need to buy. SOMA AI writes the file and reads it back to check it. The file lands in the model folder; open it in any spreadsheet app.

In the video the cut list has every board with length, width, thickness and quantity, and how its edges are finished. Edge banding is "none": the plywood edges are sanded and sealed. The shopping list has the plywood, the casters, screws, glue and finish, and even the tools to check.
steps.prompt: Make me a cut list as an Excel file: every board with its size, thickness, quantity and edge banding. Add a second sheet with a shopping list: sheet material, casters, screws and everything else I need.

image.alt: The cut list in Shelf_cut_list.xlsx: eight boards from Top to Back with quantity, length, width and thickness in mm, plywood, and the Edge banding column with none on all edges

steps.title: Change the size without the agent
text: SOMA AI made the main dimensions adjustable. Open Parameters in the sidebar: in the video there are five, the overall width, depth and height, the plywood thickness and the caster height.
Drag the width, for example from 80 to 100 cm, and the model updates right away. No agent needed for this. The height works the same way; in the video it goes from 60 to 70 cm.

image.alt: The Parameters panel with Overall width dragged to 1000 mm and the wider shelf in the 3D view

steps.title: Draw a door right on the model
text: To add something, show it. Click Mark up above the 3D view and draw on the model: in the video, the outline of a door over the left side, a line for the handle, an arrow and the word door.

Click Send to agent and add one sentence. SOMA AI first asks which hinges you have. Then it builds the door with a wooden pull and two hinges, and brings the drawings and the cut list up to date. In the video this took about 14 minutes.
steps.prompt: Add a door here, with hinges. Then update the drawings and the cut list.

image.alt: Mark up on the 3D shelf: an orange outline of a door over the left compartments, a short line for the handle, and an arrow from the word door

steps.title: Check the door, the drawings and the lists
text: In the video the door covers both left compartments, with a wooden pull. The two hinges are placeholders until you pick real ones.
The drawings now show the door and the new width of one metre, 12 sheets in all: the door and the pull have their own sheets too. The shopping list now has the hinges, a door catch and two bumpers.

image.alt: The shelf with a left-hinged door over the left side, two black hinge placeholders and a wooden pull, and SOMA AI's summary: door 49.6 cm wide and 63.1 cm high, workshop drawings with 12 sheets

tips: Write the important sizes on the sketch and say the unit (cm or mm) in your message. SOMA AI can only use what it can read.
Ask SOMA AI to ask about anything unclear before it starts. Its questions come with answers to click, so you decide the height, the material and the casters.
Say early if you may want other sizes. Then SOMA AI makes them adjustable in Parameters, and you can change them without asking again.
After a change, ask SOMA AI to update the drawings and the cut list as well, so they match the model.
Hinges and casters in the model are placeholders. Pick real products and check the sizes on the drawings before you cut.

faq.q: Can AI make furniture plans from a sketch?
faq.a: Yes. SOMA AI can read a photo of a hand sketch with sizes and turn it into a 3D model made of boards, with workshop drawings and dimensions. It works best when the sketch shows the main sizes. It asks when something is unclear, and you should still check the dimensions before you build.

faq.q: Can I get a cut list for my furniture with AI?
faq.a: Yes. Once the model is built, ask SOMA AI for a cut list as an Excel file: every board with its length, width, thickness, quantity and edge banding. You can also ask for a second sheet with a shopping list of sheet material, hardware and screws.

faq.q: Do I need CAD skills to design furniture this way?
faq.a: No. You describe the furniture in plain words, and SOMA AI builds the model. You change sizes with sliders and show changes by drawing on the model. The model is written as code, but you never have to read it.

SOMA is free and open source. SOMA AI, the agent built into it, runs on your own ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan or on an API key from a provider such as Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, which you pay for there.

faq.q: Can I change the size of the furniture later?
faq.a: Yes. If you tell SOMA AI that you may want other sizes, it makes the main dimensions adjustable. You then change width, height or depth in the Parameters panel and the model updates at once. Ask SOMA AI to update the drawings and the cut list afterwards.
